description: Defines the constraint legitimacy model. Governed structures may challenge regime constraints only through declared structural channels. Unilateral violation is classified as a violation event, not a challenge. This map specifies enforcement mechanics, challenge channel definitions, and the structural determination of legitimate versus illegitimate challenge.

constraint_legitimacy_model.formal: challenge_legitimate(S, C, R) ⟺ challenge_path(S, C, R) ⊆ declared_channels(R)

components.challenge_path: The set of structural steps taken by S in challenging C — the sequence of relations, declarations, and interactions used to contest the constraint
components.declared_channels: The enumerated set of challenge pathways declared in regime configuration R

constraint_legitimacy_model.legitimacy_determination: Legitimacy is a structural binary: a challenge is legitimate if and only if every step of its path falls within declared_channels(R). Partial channel use does not produce partial legitimacy.
constraint_legitimacy_model.tel_encoding: Challenge paths are expressible in TEL as T[challenge_ID]: S → channel_node → R, enabling formal verification by TEL-Σ and TEL-Ε.

declared_channel_types.label: Formal Objection
declared_channel_types.description: A structured declaration of constraint non-compliance sent through the regime's declared objection interface. The governed structure formally records its objection to a constraint without unilaterally violating it.
declared_channel_types.precondition: Objection interface must be declared in regime configuration
declared_channel_types.structural_effect: Objection is logged. Regime may respond with constraint clarification, suspension, or dismissal. Governed structure remains bound by the constraint during the objection period unless the regime grants a suspension.

declared_channel_types.label: Appeal
declared_channel_types.description: A challenge routed through a declared review authority above the enforcing regime node. The review authority may be a meta-regime, a peer regime, or a declared appeals body.
declared_channel_types.precondition: Review authority must be declared in regime configuration and reachable via declared structural relations
declared_channel_types.structural_effect: The constraint's enforcement is suspended pending review. If the review authority upholds the constraint, the governed structure must comply. If overturned, the constraint is removed from C_R or modified.
declared_channel_types.requires: Meta-regime or declared review authority — see INV-GRL-003

declared_channel_types.label: Renegotiation
declared_channel_types.description: A constraint modification request through the regime's declared amendment process. The governed structure proposes a revised constraint formulation acceptable to both parties.
declared_channel_types.precondition: Amendment process must be declared in regime configuration
declared_channel_types.structural_effect: If renegotiation succeeds: the constraint C in C_R is replaced with a revised constraint C'. Both the regime and the governed structure's configurations are updated. If renegotiation fails: original constraint C remains binding.
outcome_types: success: C replaced by C' in C_R
failure: C remains; governed structure must comply
deadlock: renegotiation cycle limit reached → escalate to appeal or exit

declared_channel_types.label: Exit
declared_channel_types.description: Withdrawal from the governed set through a declared exit procedure. The governed structure removes itself from S_R, ending the enforcement relation.
declared_channel_types.precondition: Exit procedure must be declared in regime configuration. Not all regimes permit exit — some may classify exit attempts as violations.
declared_channel_types.structural_effect: If exit is permitted and procedure is followed: S is removed from S_R. Enforcement relation E_R(R, S) is severed. Regime's governed-set attrition is recorded.
declared_channel_types.exit_denied_handling: If a regime does not declare an exit procedure, exit is structurally unavailable. A governed structure that attempts to exit without a declared procedure is classified as committing a violation event, not exercising a legitimate challenge.

violation_classification.description: A constraint challenge that bypasses declared channels — or any unilateral constraint non-compliance — is classified as a violation event, not a challenge.
violation_classification.formal: violation_event(S, C, R) ⟺ ¬challenge_legitimate(S, C, R) ∧ config(S) ⊭ C

violation_types.label: Unilateral Bypass
violation_types.description: Governed structure changes configuration to violate C without using any declared channel.
violation_types.enforcement_response: Standard enforcement cycle — GRL-Ε applies enforcement action; compliance response tracked for INV-GRL-002

violation_types.label: Undeclared Channel Attempt
violation_types.description: Governed structure attempts to challenge C through a path not declared in declared_channels(R) — e.g., direct negotiation bypassing the declared process, public declaration of non-compliance without objection interface.
violation_types.enforcement_response: Challenge is structurally void. Regime may treat as VT-001 and initiate standard enforcement.

violation_types.label: Meta-Regime Invocation without Standing
violation_types.description: Governed structure invokes a meta-regime as a review authority that is not declared in the regime's configuration.
violation_types.enforcement_response: Challenge is structurally void. Undeclared review authority has no standing in the regime's constraint model.

enforcement_cycle_model.description: An enforcement cycle is a discrete structural event in which the regime applies enforcement action to a governed structure regarding a specific constraint.
cycle_steps: Step 1: GRL-Ε detects configuration(S) ⊭ C for some C ∈ C_R, S ∈ S_R
Step 2: GRL-Ε applies enforcement_action(R, C, S) — a directed structural pressure signal
Step 3: GRL-Λ checks whether S has initiated a channel-based challenge: if yes, classify as legitimate_challenge; if no, classify as violation_event
Step 4: GRL-Α monitors compliance_observed(R, C, S) in the next cycle
Step 5: If compliance observed → authority α stable; if not → α decays by λ_R (INV-GRL-002)
enforcement_cycle_model.book5_integration: Enforcement actions may be expressed as TEL transformation assertions: INV[GRL-001]: assert (S ⊢ C[constraint_id]) — GRL-Ε generates and applies this assertion to the governed structure's structural record.

opacity_in_constraint_enforcement.description: When a regime's constraint set C_R carries opacity ω(C_R) > 0 (Book 4 integration), governed structures may be unable to fully identify which constraints apply to them. This creates enforcement legitimacy complications.
opacity_in_constraint_enforcement.high_opacity_effect: Governed structures cannot detect constraint boundaries → may inadvertently violate constraints → challenge legitimacy is ambiguous when governed structure claims unawareness of the constraint
opacity_in_constraint_enforcement.resolution: The structural rule is strict: opacity of C_R does not reduce the binding force of constraints. A governed structure that violates an opaque constraint is in violation, regardless of awareness. However, GRL-Λ may record the opacity level as a mitigating structural note in the enforcement record.
opacity_in_constraint_enforcement.book4_binding: INV-OR-004 (Partial Revelation) applies: governed structures may have partial access to C_R depending on their detection capacity δ and the regime's constraint-opacity profile ω(C_R)

qmroot_binding.note: Constraint legitimacy traces to Book 1 INV-002 (Constraint Preservation) and Book 5 INV-TEL-003 (Compositionality — challenge paths must be explicitly encoded). 0D only.
